title: One species, different sizes
hook: Animals can change as they grow.

doesNotKnow: Consider development when comparing identified juvenile and adult fossils.

misconception: Different-sized fossils must always be different species.
objective: Consider development when comparing identified juvenile and adult fossils.

claims.text: Animals can change as they grow. Two independently identified fossils belong to the same dinosaur species, one juvenile and one adult. What can help explain differences in their size and proportions? The schematic contrasts an identified juvenile and adult of the same stipulated species. Growth can change size and proportions; a visible difference alone does not determine whether two unidentified fossils are separate species.

claims.text: The figure is a simplified, not-to-scale schematic of a stated example, not an image of an identified specimen.
Recall: A known juvenile and adult of one species differ in size. What is one possible explanation? Individuals of the same species can differ because they are at different growth stages.
